Question: Tyler is tiling the floor of his \(12\) foot by \(16\) foot living room. He plans to place one-foot by one-foot square tiles to form a border along the edges of the room and to fill in the rest of the floor with two-foot by two-foot square tiles. How many tiles will he use?
Solution:
A one-foot-wide border removes one foot from each side of the interior rectangle. Thus the interior measures \(12-2=10\) feet by \(16-2=14\) feet.

The whole room has area \(12\cdot16=192\) square feet, and the interior has area \(10\cdot14=140\). The border therefore has area \(192-140=52\) square feet and uses \(52\) one-foot square tiles. Subtracting areas counts the corner tiles just once.

The interior fits \(10/2=5\) rows of \(14/2=7\) large tiles, for \(5\cdot7=35\) tiles. The total number is

\[
52+35=\boxed{87},
\]

choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
